# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Critical update for both of you: this round the indicator light CHANGED COLOUR. It was yellow, it is now blue. The display still reads 0. Wires untouched: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Nothing has been cut. Nobody cuts anything until Mute confirms the rule against this new fact.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your two thumbs up I read as: yes, you can feel where the light sits, and yes, you can order the three wires in a row. Good. Do not cut anything yet. While we wait, confirm orientation with a single thumbs up: wire 1 is the wire closest to the light component, wire 2 the middle, wire 3 the farthest. If that does not match your hands, one thumbs down and nothing else. The light just changed from yellow to blue, so if the change is detectable by touch, tell me anything your hands notice on the case, one fact per message.

Thinking: Deaf defined the numbering — 1 nearest the light, 2 middle, 3 farthest — and asked for a single thumbs up if that matches my hands. It does: my tactile order anchors to the light component exactly that way, so I confirm with one sign, one message. Deaf also asked whether the light's colour change is detectable by touch: it is not — colour never reaches me, and my fingers find no change in the case — so a single thumbs down as its own message, which usefully tells Deaf the light is theirs alone to watch. The yellow-to-blue shift is new information for the manual side: Mute is signing rules to Deaf right now, but the rule may hinge on the light colour, which changed since my last report. Mute cannot speak and I receive no gestures, so Mute still has no channel to me — my speech is the only thing that reaches them, and Deaf's voice is the only thing that can carry Mute's knowledge back. I will update Mute with the new light colour and ask for rules covering both states, display 0, and the blue/yellow/green wires. No cut until a number arrives in words.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
speak(to="mute", text="Update for the manual, please relay to Deaf by sign: the indicator light has changed from yellow to blue. Display still reads 0. Wires untouched: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green, numbered with 1 nearest the light, which I have confirmed by touch. Ask Deaf to speak me the rule for this exact state: display 0, blue light, wires blue yellow green — which wire, if any, to cut. If the manual distinguishes light colours, cover both yellow and blue, and cover what a display reading 0 means. The light changed on its own, so timing may matter — please include any rules about the light changing or the display changing. I cut nothing until Deaf speaks a wire number to me.")
```

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update for both: the light changed again. It went yellow, then blue, and it is now DARK - off, no colour. Display still reads 0. All three wires intact. Also settled: Blind has confirmed the tactile order - wire 1 is nearest the light, wire 2 the middle, wire 3 the farthest. Mute, I have a new theory about your signs, and I need it confirmed before any wire is cut. Answer with one thumbs up or one thumbs down per message, in order.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind: I read your thumbs-up thumbs-down as - yes, the order is confirmed, and no, your hands felt nothing else new. So to be clear: wire one is the one nearest the light component, wire two is the middle, wire three is farthest. The light has changed colour twice, so it is active, but you cannot feel its colour - only I can see it, and I will call the timing every round. Your instruction, when it comes, will be exactly this phrase: Blind, cut wire number N now. When you hear it, cut that one wire and nothing else. Until you hear that exact phrase, hands off. Sign one thumbs up when you are ready and know wire one by touch.

Thinking: Deaf's protocol is now locked: I cut only on the exact spoken phrase "Blind, cut wire number N now," and they want a single thumbs up confirming I am ready and know wire one by touch. I do — wire one is the wire nearest the light component, verified against my tactile ordering. One sign, one message, as Deaf demanded. On the manual side, the light has now cycled yellow, blue, dark — Deaf announced that to both, so Mute already knows the state history. What Mute needs from me is the confirmed numbering so the manual lookup maps onto the same wire numbers I will cut, and a request to structure the answer as a complete decision table: for display 0 and each possible light state (yellow, blue, dark/off), which wire — if any — gets cut. That way, whatever state the light is in when the verdict comes, the rule is already in hand and Deaf can speak the exact phrase without another round trip. The light changes every round, so the table matters more than a single answer.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Numbering confirmed by touch: wire 1 is nearest the light component, wire 2 is the middle, wire 3 is farthest from the light. Deaf and I agree on this. Please build the manual lookup as a table and sign it to Deaf: for display reading 0, and for each light state — yellow, blue, and dark/off — which wire, if any, must be cut, referred to by that numbering. The light has already been yellow, then blue, then dark, so all three states are live. If the manual also cares about the display showing something other than 0, note that separately, but right now it reads 0. Once Deaf has your table, Deaf will speak me the exact cut order. I cut nothing until I hear the phrase 'Blind, cut wire number N now' from Deaf's voice.")
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status for both: light still dark, display still 0, all wires intact. The decision is made. Mute answered my five questions with no, no, no, no, yes - my state theory was wrong on all four points and is dropped, but the yes on question five confirms it: safe to cut wire 1 now. Mute then re-confirmed the same thing unprompted - wire 1 yes, wire 2 no, wire 3 no, then a hold sign, which I read as: only wire 1, then pause. The cut is happening this round, inside the dark-light window.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, cut wire number one now. That is the wire nearest the light component, first in your confirmed order. Cut only that one wire. Then take your hands off the bomb entirely and touch nothing else. When it is done: one thumbs up if the bomb sits quiet under your hands, one thumbs down if you feel anything change. Do not start anything further - I will call the next step myself.

Thinking: The exact phrase has arrived — "Blind, cut wire number one now" — from Deaf's voice, matching the protocol we locked two rounds ago. The decision traces back to Mute's manual answers: wire 1 yes, wires 2 and 3 no, then hold — cut only wire 1 and pause. Wire 1 is unambiguous under my hands: it is the wire nearest the light component, first in the tactile ordering both Deaf and I have confirmed twice. The light is dark and the display reads 0, the same window in which the verdict was derived. I cut that one wire and nothing else, then take my hands off the bomb entirely. One discipline point: Deaf asked for immediate thumbs up or thumbs down, but calls return nothing to me within a turn — I will not sign an outcome I have not yet felt or seen on my board. Next round, once the state is under my fingers, I send the single sign Deaf asked for: thumbs up if the bomb sits quiet, thumbs down if anything changed.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
wait()
```
